en: The Hymn to Aparājitā
Oṃ, salutations to Aparājitā. Oṃ, for this supreme, unconquered, great vidyā belonging to Viṣṇu,
the sages are Vāmadeva, Bṛhaspati, and Mārkaṇḍeya.
The meters are Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, and Bṛhatī;
the deity is Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha;
the seed-syllables are Oṃ, Klīṃ, Śrīṃ, and Hrīṃ.
Hūṃ, the power (śakti).
For the sake of accomplishing all desires, this is the application (viniyoga) in the recitation of the Aparājita-vidyā mantra:
Oṃ, [I bow to her] who is dark like the petal of a blue lotus and adorned with serpent ornaments.
Resembling pure crystal, with a face like ten million moons. || 1 ||
The goddess Vaiṣṇavī, the unconquered, who bears the conch and the discus; the goddess who has the young moon as her crest-jewel, bestowing boons and the gesture of fearlessness. || 2 ||
Having paid homage, Mārkaṇḍeya, of great asceticism, recited this.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:

Listen, all you sages, to [the hymn of] the goddess Vaiṣṇavī, the unconquered one, who grants the fulfillment of all desires and goals, and who brings about the attainment of what has not yet been attained. (4)
Oṃ, salutations to Nārāyaṇa; salutations to the Blessed One Vāsudeva;
salutations be to Ananta, who has a thousand heads, who reclines upon the ocean of milk, whose couch is the coils of Śeṣa, whose vehicle is Garuḍa, and who is unfailing.
To the unborn, the unconquered, the one clad in yellow garments—
Oṃ Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha,
Hayagrīva, Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, Nṛsiṃha, Acyuta!
Vāmana, Trivikrama, Śrīdhara, Rāma, Rāma, Rāma! O Giver of Boons, Giver of Boons, be the Giver of Boons! Homage be unto You, homage be unto You! Svāhā!
Oṃ! [Drive away] the asuras, daityas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, siddhas, yoginīs, ḍākinīs, śākinīs, and the Skanda-grahas.
Strike, strike!
Cook, cook! Churn, churn! Destroy, destroy! Put to flight, put to flight!
Grind to powder, grind to powder! [the secondary planets, the lunar mansions, and other planets] with the conch, the discus, the thunderbolt, and the trident.
Reduce to ashes with the mace, the club, and the plow; Kuru Kuru Svāhā!
Oṃ, O thousand-armed one, O you whose weapons are a thousandfold, victory, victory! Conquer, conquer! Unconquered, immeasurable!
O Unconquered One, O Unobstructed One, O Thousand-eyed One, blaze, blaze! Flare up, flare up!
O You of Universal Form, O You of Many Forms, O Slayer of Madhu, O Great Boar!
O Great Being, Vaikuṇṭha, Nārāyaṇa, Padmanābha, Govinda, Dāmodara, Hṛṣīkeśa,
Keśava, Destroyer of all Asuras, Subduer of all beings!
The shatterer of all evil dreams, the destroyer of all mechanical devices, the subduer of all nāgas, the great lord of all gods,
the liberator from all bonds, and the crusher of all that is harmful.
O destroyer of all fevers, O warder-off of all planetary influences, O pacifier of all sins, O Janārdana, salutations be unto you, svāhā!
This mantra of Viṣṇu has been proclaimed, which bestows the fruit of all desires.
The mother who generates all good fortune, the destroyer of all fears.
Recited by all the perfected ones (siddhas), this is most dear to Viṣṇu;
there is nothing else like it for the supreme destruction of the wicked.
This secret Vidyā, belonging to Viṣṇu, is indeed called Aparājitā;
it should be recited or praised, for it is the direct refuge of the quality of goodness (sattva).
Oṃ: For the pacification of all obstacles, one should meditate upon Viṣṇu, who wears white garments, is moon-colored, has four arms, and possesses a serene countenance. 8.
Now, therefore, I shall fully describe Abhayā Aparājitā,
O child, who is considered to be my own power (śakti) consisting of the quality of rajas.

She who is manifestly composed of all beings and composed of all mantras—she who, when remembered, worshipped, recited, installed, and employed in ritual action, yields all desires; listen, my son, for I shall speak of her to you. (10)
Whoever reads this Aparājitā, the supreme Vaiṣṇavī, the unimpeded and perfected Great Knowledge (mahāvidyā), who remembers it as perfected,
recites it, chants it, hears it, remembers it, retains it, or proclaims it;

For him there shall be no fear of fire, wind, thunderbolts, stones, or showers of rain; no fear of the ocean, no fear of planetary portents, no fear of thieves, no fear of enemies, nor any fear of curses.

In some places, there shall be no fear of the darkness of night, nor of women, nor of royal families, nor of those who harbor hatred, nor of poison, sorcery, subjugation, incantations for causing enmity, eradication, killing, or imprisonment.
By means of these recited mantras— accomplished, perfected, and honored with *oṃ namo 'stu te*— [these things shall not occur].

O Fearless One, O Sinless One, O Unconquered One, O Immeasurable One, O Immortal One, O Supreme One, O Unvanquished One; O Accomplished One who recites, O Accomplished One who triumphs, O Accomplished One who remembers; O Seventy-ninth One, O Solitary One, O Mindless One.
Sudrume, Sugandhe, Ekānnaśe, Ume Dhruve, Arundhati, Gāyatri, Sāvitrī, Jātavedasi, Mānastoke, Sarasvati,
Dharaṇi, Dhāraṇi, Saudāmani, Aditi, Diti, Vinatā.
Gaurī, Gāndhārī, Mātaṅgī, Kṛṣṇe, Yaśode, Satyavādini, Brahmavādini, Kāli, Kapālini, Karālanetre, Bhadre, Nidre,
O you who fulfill true prayers! [Protect] that which has gone to the land, that which has gone to the water, and that which has gone to the atmosphere.
Or protect me from all calamities, svāhā!
For her whose flowers wither away, or whose embryo falls out;
for her whose child dies, or she who is "barren as a crow"—[protect her]. 11.
She who maintains this vidyā is not defiled by these faults;
she shall have living offspring while pregnant and shall possess sons—of this there is no doubt.
Having written this vidyā on birch bark with fragrant sandalwood, she shall not be defiled by these faults; she will become fortunate and possessed of sons. (13)
In battle, in the royal court, and in gambling, his victory shall be constant;
for the oṣā herb wards off weapons in a conflict as fierce as a storm.
It quickly destroys the pain of abdominal tumors (gulma), colic (śūla), and diseases of the eyes.
It destroys headaches and fevers for all embodied beings. || 15 ||
Thus has been declared this vidyā named Abhayā (Fearless), which is invincible;
by the mere remembrance of it, fear arises nowhere. || 16 ||
There are no calamities, nor diseases, nor warriors, nor even thieves;
there are no kings, nor serpents, nor haters, nor enemies. (17)
Neither yakṣas, rākṣasas, nor vetālas; neither śākinīs nor planetary spirits (grahas);
there is no fear of fire, nor of wind, nor of the ocean, nor indeed of poison. (18)
Whether it be a magical rite performed by an enemy, or even a rite for subjugation, expulsion, immobilization, or likewise, inciting enmity; (19)
Nothing whatsoever can prevail where this fearless [mantra] resides—whether it be recited, or present in a painting, or in a book, or even in the mouth. (20)
For the fearless person resides either in the heart or at the entrance;
one should place this [mudrā] upon the heart and meditate on the four-armed Goddess.
Wearing red garlands and garments, possessing a luster equal to a ruby, her beautiful form is adorned with the gestures of the noose, the goad, and the granting of fearlessness. || 22 ||
Bestowing even the nectar of the syllables of the mantra upon practitioners, there is nothing superior to this for subjugation. || 23 ||
It provides protection and purification; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
In the morning, young maidens should be honored with food and ornaments.
This [text] should be recited, for by pleasing them, I am pleased. (24)
Oṃ. Now, therefore, I shall fully proclaim this knowledge (vidyā) of great power, which pacifies all malevolent beings and brings about the destruction of all enemies. (25)
It pacifies the suffering of poverty and destroys misfortune and disease;
[it is the destroyer] of bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas.
She is the destroyer of ḍākinīs, śākinīs, skandas, and kūṣmāṇḍas;
she is the Great Fierce One, the Great Power, who produces immediate conviction. || 27 ||
This secret of the Lord of Pārvatī, his very soul, must be guarded with great effort;
I shall declare it to you—listen with a mind full of attention. (28)
The quotidian, the tertian, the quartan, the fortnightly, the bi-monthly, the tri-monthly, and likewise the four-monthly [fevers]. || 29 ||

It cures fever caused by wind (vāta), bile (pitta), or phlegm (śleṣman), as well as that arising from the three humors combined (sānnipātika), and likewise chronic (satata) fever, whether it has lasted for five months or six months.

The Aparājitā [mantra], when constantly remembered, swiftly destroys momentary fever, bilious fever, cold-fever, irregular fever, as well as fevers that recur every two days, every three days, or every single day. (31)
Oṃ hrīṃ hana hana, kāli śara śara, gauri dham dham,
vidye āle tāle māle gandhe bandhe paca paca vidye nāśaya nāśaya pāpaṃ hara hara saṃhāraya vā.

O destroyer of evil dreams, O mother of Vināyaka who abides upon a lotus, O you who are the twilight of the night, O you whose sound is like a drum, O you who possess the speed of mind, O bearer of the conch,
the discus, the mace, the thunderbolt, and the trident, O destroyer of untimely death!
O Sovereign of the Universe! O Draviḍī! O Drāviḍī! O Draviṇī! O Drāviṇī!
Beloved of Keśava! United with Paśupati! Subduer of the Dundubhi demon! Subduer of the excessively arrogant!
O Śabarī! O Kirātī! O Mātaṅgī! Oṃ draṃ draṃ jraṃ jraṃ kraṃ.
Kraṃ turu turu oṃ draṃ kuru kuru! Those who hate me, whether openly or in secret—all of them, subdue, subdue! Crush, crush! Torment, torment! Protect, protect!
Strike down, strike down! Dry up, dry up! Destroy, destroy!
O Brahmāṇī, Vaiṣṇavī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vārāhī, Nārasiṃhī, Aindrī, Cāmuṇḍā, Mahālakṣmī, Vaināyikī, and Aupendrī!

O fierce one of the southeast, of the southwest, of the northwest, of the north, of the northeast, protect above and below, O most formidable Knowledge! O sister of Indra and Upendra! Oṃ, homage to you, O Goddess Jaya, Vijaya, Śānti, Svasti, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Vivardhinī!
O goad of desire, O yielder of desires, O bestower of the boon of all desires!
Make me beloved among all beings, make me beloved, svāhā!
O you who attract, O you who cause possession, O you who are garlanded with flames, O delighter, O charmer!
O Upholder, O Sustainer; O Scorcher, O Inflamer; O Intoxicator, O Madder; O Drier, O Deluder!
O Blue Bannered One, O Great Blue One, O Great White One, O Great Glory! O Great Moon-like One, O Great Sun-like One, O Great Peacock-feathered One, O Solar Ray, O Jahnavī!

Yamaghaṇṭe kiṇi kiṇi Cintāmaṇi! O fragrant one, O sweet-smelling one, born from gods and asuras, you who grant all desires! May whatever task is intended according to my wish be accomplished for me, svāhā!
Oṃ svāhā | Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā | Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā |
Oṃ svaḥ svāhā | Oṃ mahaḥ svāhā | Oṃ janaḥ svāhā |
Oṃ tapas svāhā!
Oṃ satyam svāhā!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā!
"May the evil from which it came go back to that very place, svāhā! Om!
This is the unfailing great vidyā of Viṣṇu, the invincible. (32)
This Siddhi, which was personally imparted by Viṣṇu, is always accomplished through recitation;
this invincible one has been described to you as Mahābalā.
There exists no protection equal to this in the three worlds;
it is considered to be the manifest power of Rudra, consisting of the quality of darkness (tamas).
Since even Kṛtānta (Death) stands at his feet out of fear,
one should place this [mantra] at the base of the root and remember him (the deity) throughout the night.
Resembling a dark blue cloud, with tawny hair like lightning,
she is radiant as the rising sun and adorned with three eyes.
She bears a spear, a trident, a conch, and a drinking vessel;
she is clothed in a tiger skin and adorned with a network of tinkling bells. || 37 ||
She was running through the expanse of the sky with her feet placed upon a palanquin,
her face terrifying with fangs, and adorned with serpents as earrings.
With her mouth wide open and her tongue lolling, her locks of hair curved by her furrowed brow,
she drank the blood from her drinking vessel of those who hated her devotees.
She withers the seven bodily constituents by gazing with a cruel look, and she repeatedly pierces his tongue with a trident. (40)
Having bound him with a noose together with a Mānavī woman near her,
one should meditate upon the goddess Mahābalā at the time of midnight.
At the end of the night, whatever name one may utter, that yoginī brings about for each such person their corresponding state by means of the mantra recitation.
"Oṃ bale mahābale asiddhasādhanī svāhā. Thus he recites the Śrīvaiṣṇavī mantra, Amoghā, which is perfected. 43.
One should meditate upon the glorious Aparājitā-vidyā.
In the case of bad dreams, evil portents, and likewise unfavorable omens, as well as in legal disputes, success will be attained; one should recite it for the pacification of obstacles. (44)
O Mother of the World, whatever in this recitation has been praised by me lacking the visarga, the bindu, or a syllable—
may that become most complete, and may my [faults] depart.
May the fulfillment of his intentions, however, always come to pass. || 45 ||
I do not know your true nature, O Maheśvarī;
what you are like, O Great Goddess, to you who are such, salutations again and again.
